one_line: The r1 CRITICAL (prefix-collision miscompile) and all three r1 warnings are GENUINELY and SOUNDLY closed — I re-walked the F1 boundary scan against my own proven ?WG/?WG2 fixture (no 1282), traced substituted-source flow to confirm the comment-scope rationale holds (compile-only; hashes key on ORIGINAL source), and grep-confirmed the attribution and AT-range. APPROVE with ONE binding pre-code condition: tighten F4/AT-2970 ordering so the winner cross-validate fails closed BEFORE the winning-SPIR-V write (optimize.rs:104), not merely before the sidecar (optimize.rs:107) — otherwise a sibling failure strands an orphan .spv, violating §13's own 'no partial output' guarantee. This is a two-line wording+AT tightening, not a re-architecture.

r1_fix_verification.CRITICAL prefix-collision (F1) — RESOLVE: §4 F1 mandates a single left-to-right boundary-safe scan: at each `?`, match the longest assignment-set name that occurs AND whose FOLLOWING byte ∉ [A-Za-z0-9_]; else copy the byte. I walked my r1 fixture `@workgroup(?WG,1,1) shared[i32,?WG2]` {WG=128, WG2=64}: at the first `?`, `WG` occurs and is followed by `,` (boundary OK) → 128 → `@workgroup(128,1,1)`; at the second `?`, `WG` occurs but is followed by `2` (∈ident → REJECTED), `WG2` occurs and is followed by `]` (boundary OK) → 64 → `shared[i32,64]`. Output contains NO `1282`. CORRECT. Adversarial probes all pass: (a) suffix pair ?G/?WG — at `?G` only `G` occurs; at `?WG` only `WG` occurs (neither `G` nor `WG` occurs at the other's offset) → no collision, and `G` is NOT a prefix of `WG` so PrefixCollidingHoleNames does not false-positive on them; (b) `?WG2` with ONLY WG declared and `2` literal-adjacent — `WG` is rejected by the following-byte check, no other candidate matches → `?WG2` stays RAW → downstream UnresolvedStrategyHole backstop fires (fail-closed; §13 explicitly states this). CRUCIALLY the boundary check ALONE is sufficient (longest-first is belt-and-suspenders exactly as §4 states — even iterating shortest-first, `WG` is boundary-rejected at `?WG2` so `WG2` wins), and the single forward scan dissolves the ascending-BTreeMap ordering hazard by deciding each source position once. AT-2968 pins the no-1282 outcome + comment-decoy. SOUND.
r1_fix_verification.PrefixCollidingHoleNames guard coherence: The guard (union_module_holes → EnumerateError::PrefixCollidingHoleNames) rejects ONLY true prefix pairs (WG prefix-of WG2); it does NOT false-positive on legitimately co-existing non-prefix names (G/WG, WG/WGX where neither is a prefix — note WGX is NOT a prefix of WG nor vice-versa so that specific pair is fine; only WG/WG_anything-with-WG-as-literal-prefix trips it). Which layer wins WHERE is coherent and both are AT-pinned: the DISCOVERY path (autotuner/optimize via union_module_holes) fails closed at AT-2972 BEFORE substitution ever runs; the DIRECT-substitution path (rewrite-verify / compile_source_with_assignments, which never calls union_module_holes) is made correct by the F1 scan and pinned at AT-2968. The one mild asymmetry — a user MAY author independent ?WG and ?WG2 and use them via direct substitution but the autotuner will refuse them — is an intentional authoring-clarity restriction (F1 makes it sound; the guard just refuses to be confusing), and §4 states this explicitly. Coherent; not an over-restriction blocker.
r1_fix_verification.Comment-scope rationale — RESOLVED and i: The spec argues a substituted `?WG`-in-comment is harmless because the lexer discards comments before HIR, so it cannot change SPIR-V / hole resolution / golden bytes. I additionally TRACED where the substituted String flows to close the sharper question (can it perturb source-hash-keyed artifacts?): substitute_strategy_holes has exactly two live callers — compile_source_with_assignments (lib.rs:262 → feeds compile_source_with_meta, a transient local String consumed by the pipeline) and fuzz.rs:895 (feeds the front end). Neither PERSISTS the substituted output. The source-hash-keyed artifacts key on the ORIGINAL user source, NOT the per-variant substituted text: MCP grid_search hashes `xxh3_64(source.as_bytes())` on the request source (grid_search.rs:381) and history_path_for_source(dir, &source) uses that same original source (grid_search.rs:384) — it MUST, else every variant would fork a distinct history file. M3.19 log-opt fails closed on multikernel before any splice and operates on the original .axc file bytes (not substituted output). M3.16 rewrite round-trip compares rewritten-vs-original source; substitution is a downstream compile-only transient outside that byte-verbatim path. CONCLUSION: substituted source is strictly compile-scoped; a comment substitution can reach NO hash or byte-span. The rationale HOLDS, and the asymmetry vs the lexer-anchored STRIP path (whose comment decoy CAN remove the wrong block) is correctly reasoned. VERIFIED.
r1_fix_verification.Wrong-metadata hazard — RESOLVED, wrap i: §8's compile_source_with_meta_kernel doc-contract mandates building ONE `HirModule{kernels: vec![selected.clone()]}` and threading THAT module through BOTH emit_module_bytes(&one,…) AND the entire metadata block (extract_workgroup_dims(&one), one.kernels.first(), shared-bytes, coopmat). The §5 table now lists extract_workgroup_dims (codegen/lib.rs:42) and the lib.rs:153 first() read. AT-2969 uses DISTINCT per-kernel workgroup dims and asserts the --kernel-selected non-first kernel's sidecar carries ITS OWN workgroup_size AND entry_point — which AT-2950 cannot catch (the shipped example shares ?WG). compile_source_with_meta[_debug] delegate with kernel=None so single-kernel golden (AT-2947) is byte-identical (one = the sole kernel = the raw hir). AIRTIGHT.
r1_fix_verification.strip_all termination — RESOLVED, provab: §8/F2 pins the predicate to `prev != next` (while the last strip CHANGED the source), NOT 'while a @strategy token exists'. I confirmed strip_strategy_annotation_block returns the source UNCHANGED for the call-form @strategy(...) (lib.rs:395-398 — trimmed does not start with `{`) and for an unmatched brace (lib.rs:425). Each iteration therefore either removes exactly one brace-form block (source strictly SHRINKS) or is a no-op (prev==next → loop halts on first no-op). No pathological input can loop forever: monotone strict decrease bounded below by the no-op fixpoint. SOUND. AT-2955 gates it.
r1_fix_verification.at_2835 block-count branch — RESOLVED, e: I read the anchor (lib.rs:911-996). It has two clauses per @strategy-bearing file: (1) `robust == naive_strip_reference` byte-equality, and (2) a residual no-live-`@strategy {` check. For two_pass_reduce.axc (2 blocks): clause (1) STILL HOLDS because BOTH naive_strip_reference (source.find first) and strip_strategy_annotation_block (lexer-anchored first) strip only the FIRST block, identically → equal (the spec is right). Clause (2) is what breaks (2nd block survives single-block strip). §5's fix branches ONLY clause (2) on block count — strip_all_… residual check for >1-block files — while keeping clause (1) unchanged for ALL files (the load-bearing OLD-vs-NEW pin is never weakened). AT-2971 gates it. Correct. (Impl note for the Coder, non-blocking: count NON-COMMENT brace-form blocks so matmul_f32_tiled.axc's comment decoy at line 13 doesn't misroute; even if it did, only clause (2) is affected and strip-all still leaves no residual, so matmul stays green — the design is robust to a mis-count.)

warnings: WARNING / F4 ORDERING PRECISION (binding pre-code condition — the ONE residual): §4 F4 and AT-2970 both say the winner cross-validate must 'fail closed BEFORE writing the winner SIDECAR.' But run_optimize (optimize.rs) does TWO writes: the winning SPIR-V at optimize.rs:104 (`std::fs::write(output, &spv_bytes)`) THEN the strategy sidecar at optimize.rs:107-109. A literal reading of 'before the sidecar' permits placing the cross-validate between line 104 and 107 — which would STRAND an orphan out.spv on the disk when a sibling kernel fails to compile/validate, contradicting §13's own 'no partial output' fail-closed guarantee (the compile path explicitly promises 'no file written' on AmbiguousKernel). AT-2970 as worded ('fails closed BEFORE writing the sidecar') would PASS the orphan-.spv implementation, so the test does NOT gate the discipline. FIX (Architect wording, ~2 lines): F4 must fail closed BEFORE the winning-SPIR-V write at optimize.rs:104 (equivalently: cross-validate the winner across ALL kernels immediately after computing winner_assignments, before ANY write); AT-2970 must additionally assert that NO out.spv AND no sidecar exists after a sibling-failure fail-closed. This is a precision tightening of a fix I introduced in r1 — the DESIGN (cross-validate via compile_module_all before declaring victory) is correct; only the write-ordering phrasing is loose. Non-blocking for architecture; MUST be corrected in the spec text (or explicitly honored by the Coder) so the no-partial-output discipline stays airtight on the optimize path as it is on the compile path.

primary_risk_reassessment: UNCHANGED from r1 and still not a blocker. The Architect's stated PRIMARY RISK (a while-stride barrier tripping OQ2) is over-stated (OQ2 fires only on conditional_depth>0; while/for-range bodies bump divergent_context_depth, not conditional_depth, so a workgroup-uniform barrier at while-body top level passes both OQ2 and the collective check). The residual honest concern is OQ1's missing-barrier SET analysis across the loop back-edge, and the spec's FALLBACK (pin ?WG to one candidate + fully unroll, mirroring the proven shared_reduce.axc) is a real, buildable safety net that still demonstrates the cross-kernel binding at compile time (AT-2956). §6.1 explicitly leaves the looped-vs-unrolled resolution to the Coder against the real analyzers; either satisfies the milestone. Sound.

summary: APPROVE (cycle 2 of 3). Every r1 item is genuinely closed and I verified each against the actual source rather than taking the changelog's word: (1) the CRITICAL prefix-collision miscompile is fixed by F1's boundary-safe single-scan — I re-walked it against my own proven ?WG/?WG2 fixture and confirmed the following-byte guard alone yields shared[i32,64] with NO 1282, plus all adversarial probes (suffix pairs, undeclared-WG2-with-literal-2, prefix-guard false-positive) resolve correctly and fail-closed; (2) the comment-scope rationale HOLDS and I strengthened its justification by tracing that substituted source is compile-scoped only — the two callers never persist it and every source-hash-keyed artifact (grid_search xxh3/history, log-opt spans, rewrite round-trip) keys on the ORIGINAL source, so a comment substitution can perturb no hash; (3) the wrong-metadata wrap threads ONE 1-kernel HirModule through both emit and metadata with a distinct-dims AT-2969 that AT-2950 cannot catch; (4) strip_all's `prev!=next` predicate provably terminates; (5) at_2835's block-count branch preserves the load-bearing equality clause unweakened; (6) the attribution is grep-confirmed (enumerate_variants is the sole liar; load_source is silent-pick).
